subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat streamed replies and precise pairing states

question: Should Linux Quick Chat become a full in-place reply surface for every accepted Gateway chat outcome, including cached-complete retries and BTW side results, rather than only normal streamed agent replies?
rationale: The patch expands a previously send-and-open-dashboard shortcut into a persistent reply UI; the protected maintainer label means the desired scope and presentation policy should be confirmed alongside the bounded correctness repairs.

options.title: Sponsor the complete reply surface
options.body: Keep the feature and require the two lifecycle repairs so every accepted Quick Chat send reaches a visible terminal state.

options.title: Narrow to normal streamed runs
options.body: Limit the initial feature to normal agent streaming and explicitly remove or defer unsupported accepted-send outcomes from the UI contract.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause this broad Linux UX expansion until a maintainer defines the intended Quick Chat session and reply model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the complete reply surface
recommendation.body: Keep the feature and require the two lifecycle repairs so every accepted Quick Chat send reaches a visible terminal state.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch and Linux Quick Chat implementation history in this review are concentrated in these commits.
